notes: Owner's decision 2026-10-11 (docs/decisions/2026-10-11-when-stylebro-goes-stable.md): 1.0 ships after two clean trials in a row, first-run trials on new kinds of repository with no high-severity bugs; external users aren't required. Tally: 0 in a row after trial 42 (2026-10-22; owner: "Not clean"): BRO1151 expanded `Task.WhenEach([a, b, c])` on PolyShim's C# 14 extension-member polyfill and the compiler reported CS8620 for the elements (6 errors with warnings as errors), and PolyShim's build runs a file-based program (`dotnet run` of GenerateSignatures.csx) that got StyleBro from the root Directory.Build.props and failed on 37 findings `format` can't fix; format and check named neither (`bro check --build` caught both). Also fixed: init, format and the preview stopped at their first MSBuild query on PolyShim (MSB4184: an item condition only a build skips), the preview left out kiota-dotnet's in-solution-generator configuration gap, and check --build said "Not verified" for IDE0049 on sbom-tool although its builds enforce it (owner's choices: file-based programs get no StyleBro analyzers; such builds count as the check). Held up: N_m3u8DL-RE (random, seed 42), sbom-tool (StyleCop, migrate) and kiota-dotnet converged in one run, preview matched format file by file, TWAE builds and tests matched the untouched code; trial 41's BRO1509/BRO1139/BRO1519 fixes held in a spot repro. Before: Tally: 1 in a row after trial 41 (2026-10-21; owner: "Count it clean"): PolygonClipper (StyleCop from its shared-infrastructure submodule, migrate), Havit.Blazor (Razor, init) and ClosedXML (random, seed 41) converged in one run; preview, format, check and check --build agreed before and after committing (exit 3 only for IDE0049 held back on SDK 10.0.113), and TWAE builds and tests matched the untouched code. Trial 40's fixes held (migrate wrote into src/ and tests/.editorconfig, which the build doesn't overwrite; x64/x86 and Release configurations checked). Fixed: BRO1139 and BRO1519 gave ClosedXML a different blank line depending on fix order (preview and format disagreed in 2 files), and BRO1509 expanding a one-line member with attributes on its line needed a second run (spot check; the formatter moves the attributes). Before: 0 in a row after trial 40 (2026-10-21; owner: "Not clean"): ImageSharp.Web's build copies its shared-infrastructure submodule's .editorconfig over the root one, so migrate's block was gone after the first build and the TWAE build reported 897 findings format and check had called clean (`bro check --build` caught it); `check --build` run before committing format's changes said a false "Not clean" (the HEAD copy's library failed on BRO findings, so the code's own errors in projects referencing it counted as new) and named a project unchecked in Release as one that didn't compile; BRO1102's `[A] [B]` needed a second plain `dotnet format` run. All fixed; trial 39's submodule, using-group and unbuilt-project fixes held. Before: 0 in a row after trial 39 (2026-10-21; owner: "Not clean"): MailKit (random, seed 39) builds its MimeKit submodule's project through MailKit.sln, and with StyleBro in the root props that build reported 145,994 findings `format` leaves alone, while format and check named only IDE0049 as unchecked (`bro check --build` caught it); migrate mapped Open-XML-SDK's blankLinesBetweenUsingGroups to dotnet_separate_import_directive_groups = true and the first format added blank lines to 342 StyleCop-clean files; StronglyTypedId's projects no configuration builds were listed as "Not checked"; all fixed (a superproject's solution hides submodule projects' findings, migrate follows the code for using groups: owner's choices; the runs leave out not-built projects). Held up: all four converged in one run, TWAE builds and tests matched the untouched code, dunet's CSharpier check named only the file CSharpier rejected before, Open-XML-SDK's PublicAPI files and snapshot tests stayed intact. Before: 1 in a row after trial 38 (2026-10-21; owner: "Count it clean"): AwesomeAssertions (migrate, StyleCop only in its net8.0 build), MagicOnion (init, in-solution generator), microsoft/vs-solutionpersistence (migrate, Directory.Build.rsp; a spot copy with /Restore) and git-credential-manager (random) converged in one run; preview, format, check and check --build agreed, and builds and tests matched the untouched code. Two spot-only findings were fixed: BRO1113 removed MarkdownSnippets regions referenced as `Snippet:`, from `.mdx` pages or through `include:` (mdsnippets failed "Missing snippet"), and a public-API approval file held 127 private-field renames in an AwesomeAssertions copy with `_camelCase` (owner: API listings hold public names only). Before: 0 in a row after trial 37 (2026-10-20; owner: "Not clean"): MSBuildSdks' Directory.Build.rsp says /Restore, so bro's own MSBuild queries restored with a forced target framework and left two netstandard2.0 projects a net9.0 restore output (NU1109): `dotnet format` couldn't load them, format and check said "Not verified" and the TreatWarningsAsErrors build failed on 4 findings there (`bro check --build` caught it); BRO1113 removed two MarkdownSnippets regions in shouldly and its build failed ("Missing snippet"), which no bro verdict reported; renames changed code Shouldly quotes in its failure messages (37 of 1,122 tests failed); all fixed (queries pass -restore:false; snippet regions stay and the renamers keep names snapshot files or, with Shouldly, strings of the file quote: owner's choices). Held up: preview, format, check and check --build agreed on every repository (Not verified, exit 3, IDE0049 held back on SDK 10.0.113), the lens-2 spot repro named the projects a failed one kept from compiling, Xunit.Combinatorial (StyleCop 1.2, migrate) changed nothing. Before: 0 in a row after trial 36 (2026-10-20; owner: "Not clean"): `bro format` silently left out NodaTime's lib/commandline/*.cs (compiled by a project from above src/, the solution's folder), `bro check` called the rest clean, and the TreatWarningsAsErrors build failed on 134 StyleBro findings there (`bro check --build` caught it); `bro preview` said "clean after 1 run" and exited 0 where format said "Not verified" (SharpZipLib, NodaTime, WireMock.Net); in a spot repro `bro check --build` said "Clean" when a project a failed one needed never compiled; all fixed (format formats such files, the preview ends like format, --build names uncompiled projects: owner's choices). PR #266's gaps held: IDE0049 held back with exit 3 on SDK 10.0.113, an old-style net48 project named as not loaded; C-Sharp-Algorithms (random) clean. Before: 0 in a row after trial 35 (2026-10-20; owner: "Not clean"): `bro format` stopped at the restore on sqlite-net (a multi-targeted project with a net8.0-ios framework and no iOS workload); the SDK's IDE0049 wrote `using X = nint;` into sqlite-net's SQLite.cs, which a netstandard2.0 library compiles with C# 7.3 (CS8370), and the multi-target guard that should hide such fixes is ignored by SDK 10.0.113's `dotnet format` for IDE rules; BRO1606 left `class.</c>.` in Castle Core's doc comments (32 CS1570); BRO1304 renamed nested interfaces that Castle Core's tests name in strings (`Tests+PrivateInterface`, 6 failures); all fixed (format leaves such projects alone, passes the guard the files an older C# compiles and holds the guard's IDE fixes back where `dotnet format` ignores suppressors: owner's choices). Trial 34's fixes held (#if opening `try {` in ExcelDataReader, BRO1008's skips in Castle Core, an unlisted reference in a MemoryPack spot copy). Before: 0 in a row after trial 34 (2026-10-19; owner: "Not clean"): `bro format` never settled on netmq (a `try {` that `#if DEBUG` opens: the Debug and Release runs re-indented the statement inside it every run) while `bro check` said clean; on protobuf-net format said "Clean" above a BRO1008 warning no fix could change (the TreatWarningsAsErrors build reports it), skipped protobuf-net.Test in its net8.0 run (a referenced project the solution filter doesn't list) and counted a CRLF line-ending artifact as an IDE0055 finding; all fixed (BRO1008 now skips such files, owner's choice). Trial 33's fixes held (lone CRs, xUnit 1.24+, BRO1405 query alignment); the runtime-style run (complog, `init --style microsoft --write`) matched its baseline. Before: 0 in a row after trial 33 (2026-10-19; owner: "Not clean"): `bro format` left taglib-sharp's and Scriban's files with a lone CR out, still said "Clean" (exit 0, `bro check` too), and the TreatWarningsAsErrors build failed on them; with xunit.analyzers 1.24+ (Tmds.DBus) format said Clean where check said Not clean (its fixes have no Fix All from 1.24 on); BRO1405 left a query's clauses misaligned, so Ix.NET needed a second run; all fixed. The runtime-style run (Tmds.DBus, `init --style microsoft --write`) matched its baseline. Before: 0 in a row after trial 32 (2026-10-18; owner: "Not clean"): init's end_of_line = lf converted RazorLight's CRLF test files, whose multi-line verbatim strings then held LF, and two rendering tests failed; format skipped two CAP samples in its net10.0 run (transitive references), needed a second run in Pinta (BRO1132 with K&R braces, BRO1504 with tab_width 8), and migrate re-indented ControlzEx's case blocks; all fixed. Trial 33 must include a dotnet/runtime-style repository run with `bro init --style microsoft` (owner's decision 2026-10-18, "Lens in trial 33"): the Microsoft style (backlog 075, docs/styles.md) has never been trialed on code that follows the runtime's conventions. Before: 0 in a row after trial 31 (2026-10-18; owner: "Not clean"): init marked Hangfire's whole repository as vendored code (a GPL COPYING next to its own LICENSE.md), so StyleBro would have formatted nothing there, and the renames changed 8 Avalonia property registration fields in Ursa.Avalonia (AVP1022); both fixed. Before: 1 clean in a row after trial 30 (2026-10-18; owner: "Count it clean"): Chell, rwmt/Multiplayer, QuestPDF and AvaloniaVisualBasic6 converged in one run with builds and tests as on the untouched code; the one bug (format stopped at the restore on Android/iOS/Browser heads without their workloads) changed nothing and is fixed.
